The constraint we start with

What slows e-commerce teams down.

We begin with the moments where people wait, repeat work, or lose context. Then we automate the predictable part and keep judgment with the right person.

01

Returns to origin eat the margin

COD orders refused at the door, unreachable buyers and incomplete addresses send parcels back after paying freight both ways. Failed delivery attempts are reported late and rarely verified with the shopper before the courier gives up.

02

Listings drift across channels

The same product reads differently on the D2C store, Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Nykaa and quick-commerce apps. Mandatory declarations go missing, stock counts disagree and popular SKUs oversell.

03

Support answers the same questions all day

Where is my order, will this fit, which shade suits me, how do I claim warranty. Sale days overwhelm the team, and answers drift away from the published policy.

04

Messaging without consent backfires

Blanket WhatsApp and SMS campaigns sent without opt-in invite blocks, paused templates, DND complaints and regulatory attention. Shoppers stop listening to the brand.

05

The rules on prices, consent and listings are tightening

The amended E-Commerce Rules, the CCPA dark-pattern guidelines, Legal Metrology listing requirements and the DPDP Rules all shape how discounts, consent, data and listings must work. Manual processes leave little evidence of how each rule is followed.

06

Retention runs on discounts

Repeat purchase is where D2C economics work, yet most journeys are generic sale blasts. Replenishment timing, size and shade preferences and the post-purchase experience go unused.

The perfect automation

Order-to-doorstep assurance for COD-heavy stores

One connected flow from the moment an order is placed to the moment it is delivered: COD and address confirmation on WhatsApp, risk-based holds reviewed by a person, proactive shipping updates, and fast resolution of failed delivery attempts. It targets a familiar leak for COD-heavy stores in India, parcels that travel to a door and come back, without putting obstacles in front of genuine buyers.

  1. 01

    Capture and score every order

    Order webhooks from Shopify or the OMS reach the workflow within seconds. Rules check the address against the pincode serviceability master and score risk from order value, payment mode, pincode return history and past refusals.

    nn8nPPythonSSupabase
  2. 02

    Confirm the order on WhatsApp

    Shoppers who opted in to WhatsApp order updates at checkout get an approved utility template to confirm the order and address with one tap, edit the address or cancel. Undelivered messages and shoppers without opt-in fall back to a DLT-registered SMS service template or an IVR call.

    WBWhatsApp Business Platformnn8n
  3. 03

    Hold risky orders for a person

    Unconfirmed, high-risk and high-value orders wait in a review queue with the evidence and a call script. The reviewer releases, calls the shopper or cancels.

    RRetoolSSupabase
  4. 04

    Keep the shopper informed

    Courier events become clear shipped and out-for-delivery updates with a tracking link, so shoppers expect the parcel and fewer where-is-my-order tickets reach support.

    WBWhatsApp Business Platformnn8n
  5. 05

    Resolve failed attempts before cut-off

    When a courier reports a failed delivery (NDR), the shopper gets the stated reason and options within minutes on an approved template; the chosen reattempt slot or corrected address goes back through the courier's NDR API or panel before the cut-off.

    WBWhatsApp Business Platformnn8nSSupabase
  6. 06

    Learn by pincode, channel and campaign

    Confirmation, NDR and return-to-origin outcomes flow into a warehouse model and dashboard, so growth and operations teams can adjust COD availability, courier allocation and campaigns with evidence.

    GBGoogle BigQueryddbtMPMicrosoft Power BI

Human checkpoint

An order-operations reviewer decides on every held, high-value or disputed order and every cancellation the shopper did not request; the logistics lead escalates disputed courier NDR reasons. The system never cancels an order or switches off COD for a pincode on its own.

What changes

  • Fewer parcels shipped to unreachable or unwilling buyers, and lower return-to-origin freight
  • Failed delivery attempts verified with the shopper and resolved before the courier returns the parcel
  • Fewer where-is-my-order contacts reaching the support team
  • Clear evidence on where COD, couriers and campaigns create avoidable returns

Automation playbook

Start where the work repeats.

A selection from the playbook. Each blueprint shows the trigger, steps, tools, human checkpoint, data handling, deliverables, and measures.

Discover · 4–6 weeks

AI catalog enrichment with mandatory-field checks

Turn supplier sheets, pack photos and spec documents into complete, channel-ready listings. AI drafts titles, attributes and descriptions from approved facts, rules check mandatory declarations, and a category owner approves every listing before it goes live.

View the blueprint ↗Discover · 5–8 weeks

Stock, price and batch sync across every sales channel

Keep sellable stock, prices and offers consistent across the D2C store, marketplaces and quick-commerce partners. Buffers prevent overselling, near-expiry batches are held back or proposed for markdown, and rate-linked prices such as gold jewelry are recalculated for approval.

View the blueprint ↗Discover · 3–5 weeks

Creator collaboration and ad-disclosure workflow

Run creator and influencer programs from brief to repost with clear records: product seeding, approved claims sheets, disclosure checks, usage rights and sales by creator code. Built for beauty brands, where claims and disclosure draw close scrutiny.

View the blueprint ↗Evaluate · 5–7 weeks

Grounded fit, shade and spec advisor

Answer pre-purchase questions on size and fit, shade and skin type, or technical specs using only the brand's own size charts, shade guides, spec sheets and policies. When the answer is not in the approved sources, the assistant says so and hands over to a person.

View the blueprint ↗Evaluate · 3–5 weeks

Video and showroom consultation booking

Let shoppers book a video call or showroom visit with a designer or jewelry consultant, pass the right product context to the consultant beforehand, and send follow-ups, quotes and approved financing information after the call.

View the blueprint ↗Checkout and confirm · 2–4 weeks

Consented cart and checkout recovery

Follow up abandoned carts only with shoppers who opted in, on the channel they chose, with honest messages: no fake countdowns, no pre-added items, the total price including fees shown upfront, and a clear way to opt out.

How we work

A clear delivery rhythm, from discovery to daily operation.

Five phases with named deliverables, client inputs, and review points. Most teams start with a focused pilot.

  1. 01 · 1–2 weeksDiscover

    We map how orders, listings and conversations actually flow today across channels, the OMS, couriers, the helpdesk and consent records. We sample orders, RTO and NDR history, return reasons and support tickets to find where money and time leak, and agree which journey to fix first.

  2. 02 · 1–2 weeksDesign

    We design each flow end to end: triggers, rules, message templates, review queues and data handling. Templates are drafted for WhatsApp category approval and DLT registration, discount and urgency wording is checked against the dark-pattern guidelines, and every decision point names the person who owns it.

  3. 03 · 2–5 weeksBuild

    We build in short increments on the agreed stack, usually n8n or Node.js workflows, a Supabase data layer, Retool review consoles and the client's existing messaging providers. Integrations use official APIs, credentials are kept in a secrets vault, and every workflow logs what it did and why.

  4. 04 · 1–2 weeksValidate & launch

    We test normal and failure paths with realistic orders: undelivered messages, courier API errors, partial stock, wrong addresses and opt-outs. AI answers are scored against approved sources. Launch is staged by channel, pincode set or share of orders, with a rollback switch, and avoids peak sale days.

  5. 05 · Ongoing, with monthly reviewsOperate & improve

    After launch we watch the numbers with you: RTO, NDR resolution, handoff rates, opt-outs and failures. Monthly reviews retire messages that do not earn their place, update knowledge sources when policies change, and prepare the stack before sale events.

Suggested first pilot

COD confirmation and failed-delivery resolution pilot

A focused four-week pilot on one storefront and one courier aggregator: WhatsApp confirmation for COD and flagged orders, a review queue for held orders, and NDR follow-up before the courier cut-off. Results are compared with a holdout group of orders, so both teams can see what changed before scaling.

  • One storefront or OMS and one courier aggregator connected
  • COD and address confirmation on WhatsApp with SMS or IVR fallback
  • Risk rules and a review queue for held and high-value orders
  • NDR follow-up loop with reattempt instructions sent back to the courier
  • Holdout-based report on confirmation, NDR resolution and RTO

Measures

Know whether it is working.

Proposed measures, agreed with your team before launch, with a source, owner, and review cadence.

Return-to-origin (RTO) rate

Share of shipped orders returned to origin without delivery, split by payment mode, pincode, courier and campaign.

COD confirmation rate

Share of COD orders confirmed by the shopper before dispatch, out of all COD orders created in the period.

NDR resolution before cut-off

Share of failed delivery attempts where a shopper response and courier instruction were recorded before the courier's reattempt cut-off.

Listing completeness

Share of live SKUs with every mandatory declaration and required channel attribute present and approved.
